title: Compose durable owner-grant authority and host worker enforcement
description: Owner: cross-account-sharing; integration partner monitoring-central (PR58 owner). Depends on delegation contract and separately coordinated hosted integration. Durable conditional grant/revocation/audit/request reservations, fresh owner/consumer authority, guarded execution, immutable billing attribution and caller-specific receipt access. Never convert sharing into owner membership or console:write. Test concurrency, revocation during execution/disclosure, uncertain provider reconciliation and private history exclusion. Production target approval and credentials remain pending. Does not block original four-output priming.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Hosted integration preparation remains isolated from the main owner's merged PR58/bootstrap paths. This task owns new publication_sharing_storage.py and adjacent specifications; new publication_sharing_authorization.py and adjacent specifications; cross-module tests/publication_sharing_integration_test.py; and updates to docs/publication-sharing.md. No runtime, worker, console, account-route, bootstrap, infrastructure or credential files are claimed.

Use the existing canonical Journal/S3Journal, not a new persistence system. One explicitly initialized, bounded owner-and-engine ledger commits grants, quotas, requests, source pins and audit atomically through one conditional head write. Never retry transaction bodies or turn uncertain commit acknowledgements into dispatch authority. Every transaction reads current canonical state. Missing/corrupt state, mismatched ownership, exhausted limits or storage outages fail closed.

Request-local host authentication must re-resolve the verified session and central account authority at every effect boundary. Issue/revoke requires exact owner role plus a separate exact engine/grant-management approval callback; admin/member/console:write alone is insufficient. Consumer membership requires an additional explicit publication-and-operation authorization callback. No new grants, authentication authority, endpoints or production credentials are deployed by this source preparation.

Feature: Durable and freshly authorized publication sharing
Scenario: Concurrent last allowance
Given two processes reading one remaining grant allowance in the canonical journal
When both reserve different requests
Then only one conditional transaction commits
And only its confirmed reservation may dispatch provider work
Scenario: Lost commit acknowledgement
Given a reservation or disclosure commit whose outcome becomes uncertain
When the worker restarts or retries the same request
Then no additional paid call is authorized
And the original reservation and audit remain available for explicit reconciliation
Scenario: Current owner authority
Given a valid session with owner, admin, member or viewer role
When it requests grant management
Then only the current owner with explicit exact-scope grant authority succeeds
And role, session, publication or operation changes fail closed
Scenario: Durable addressed delivery
Given one existing central decision and a current consumer-authorized delivery grant
When its scoped receipt is delivered, the service restarts, and the receipt is requested again
Then source and decision provenance survive
And no repeated classification occurs
And revocation prevents subsequent disclosure

All acceptance tests use synthetic identities, fake account transport, local or synthetic conditional journal storage and an offline native model. npm/pip install, download and cache operations remain held for cleanup. Source reviews and remote CI continue; real identity mapping does not block these tests.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Source preparation implemented in new publication_sharing_storage.py, publication_sharing_authorization.py and adjacent specs, plus tests/publication_sharing_integration_test.py. No main-owner runtime, worker, console, bootstrap, infrastructure or credential files changed. The existing journal/account/native modules imported by this implementation are identical between the declared develop base and merged PR58 main.

The canonical S3 journal adapter pins owner/workspace/engine, performs one conditional commit per transaction, retains grant/quota/source/request/audit atomically, never retries transaction bodies, invalidates uncertain handles and reserves revocation capacity. The account adapter pins a verified request session, uses exact owner role plus explicit grant scope, and checks consumers only against their own account read membership plus publication/operation scope. Neither adapter installs a new production authority.

Final focused verification passed 312 tests: 118 core sharing, 40 durable storage, 70 request authorization, eight composed service/native-engine cases and 76 existing account/journal neighbors. Specs were run red before implementation. Ruff/format, diff check and Kanbus validation pass. The independent cross-repository smoke also passes real adapter/native-engine composition through the existing Papyrus handoff into a separate internal native Cyclotron: one original central call and one internal call, no duplicate central work; receipt possession alone cannot read source data, and revocation prevents subsequent reads/dispatch. The smoke uses synthetic in-process transport, not a deployed HTTP claim.

The previous PR60 head 4b50f88d774e1617606041a70fcc89dd84f27156 has terminal passing test/diagrams CI in run39444088412. Papyrus PR388 head17d8b6ba11d456b7bb5aede163d2a4a10b2582de has terminal passing Python/TS/package-smoke CI in runs39444134087 and39444134074. The new PR60 source head will be verified separately after publication.

No production ledger, grant, route, new authentication authority, credentials, site or infrastructure was provisioned.
